title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Price increase (1.5%)
drivers.evidence: Historical $0.68 weeks show a noise-adjusted median of x0.95 vs baseline; 2026-09-28: 524 (12% above), 2026-10-05: 388 (11% below); average effect: -5% after noise adjustment.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: Past heat events (35°C+) show no consistent lift; 2026-07-20 (35°C): 435 (1% above); 2026-08-10 (33°C): 480 (10% above); no clear demand drop in heat. However, 38°C exceeds prior max, and heat may reduce consumption. Estimate downside based on uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 438.2. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increased slightly to $0.68 (+1.5%), but historical data shows no significant price sensitivity: past $0.68 weeks (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) had medians of 524 and 388, with a noise-adjusted effect of x0.95 vs baseline (down 5%). The heatwave (38°C) may reduce demand, as high temps correlate with lower produce sales in past data (e.g., 2026-07-20: 435 at 35°C; 2026-08-10: 480 at 33°C). No strong evidence of heat-driven demand shift, but caution is warranted. The classical uplift model suggests no change, consistent with limited historical signal. Adjust downward modestly for price and heat.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 0.68 (+1.5% vs regular price 0.67)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.2 | 5%-95%: 312.6 - 556.1 | 10%-90%: 346.5 - 529.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
